beats.say: One angle. That is how a sunflower packs its seeds. Watch what happens when it's wrong.

head: THE RULE:
TURN, PLACE, REPEAT.
beats.say: The rule: place a seed, turn by a fixed angle, step out a little, repeat. Seven hundred times.

head: TURN 90°:
4 ARMS.
beats.say: Turn a quarter turn each time and you get four straight arms. Huge gaps.

head: TURN 137°:
SO CLOSE.
beats.say: Try a hundred and thirty seven degrees. Spirals, but still gaps.

head: THE GOLDEN
ANGLE.
beats.say: Now the golden angle, about 137.5 degrees. No gaps. Every seed fits.
beats.speak: Now the golden angle, about a hundred and thirty seven and a half degrees. No gaps. Every seed fits.

head: REAL SUNFLOWERS
DO THIS.
beats.say: Real sunflowers grow in spirals like these. Count them and you usually get two Fibonacci numbers, like 21 going this way and 34 going that way.
beats.speak: Real sunflowers grow in spirals like these. Count them and you usually get two Fibonacci numbers, like twenty one going this way and thirty four going that way.

beats.say: Follow Ship With Pip for more.

title: 137.5 degrees: the one angle that packs a sunflower
caption: 700 seeds, one rule: place a seed, turn by a fixed angle, step out, repeat. Turn 90° and you get 4 straight arms. 137° and 138° leave gaps. The golden angle, about 137.5°, packs every seed with no gaps. Real sunflowers grow in spirals like these, and the spiral counts are almost always two consecutive Fibonacci numbers, like 21 and 34.
notes: Golden angle = 360 * (1 - 1/phi) = 137.508 degrees (stats). Seed i at radius c*sqrt(i+0.5), angle i*turn. Science News: golden angle about 137.5 degrees; sunflower with 21 clockwise and 34 counterclockwise spirals; spiral counts almost always two consecutive Fibonacci numbers.
